area: Water rules: waterStatus, the water part of findExceptions, waterMultiples and the "Water tanks OK" tile
summary:
On the committed data the water rules give exactly the three planted alerts, with correct text and correct "here now" context. The existing 8 tests pass. When the input is less tidy, the rules break in several reproduced ways. These are the most serious:
(1) If a tank has no readings in the last 7 days, waterMultiples crashes. The water, grazing, gain, budget and rules sections all go blank (B-01).
(2) level_pct is never validated. An "ERR" reading on T2's newest row removes T2's critical alert and counts the tank as OK (W-10, B-05). A blank level becomes a false "Dropped 80 points in 24 hours, now %" (W-09).
(3) There is no tank master table, so a tank with zero rows disappears from the alerts, the chart grid and the tile ("5 of 7") (W-08, B-02).
(4) Rows are ordered by string comparison of timestamps. A water.csv re-saved by Excel (m/d/yyyy) picks Sep 9 as every tank's "last" reading: 8 false "No reading for 516 hours" rows, and the real T2 and T4 problems are hidden (W-05b).
(5) drop24h's baseline is "the latest reading at least 24 h before the last reading", with no upper age limit and no fallback. After a sensor outage, a 3-day change is reported as "in 24 hours" and triggers a critical leak alarm (W-01). A 45-point fall over 18 h of history raises nothing (W-02).
(6) A reading dated after as_of gives a negative silentHours and passes as fresh. One mistyped row hides T6's 42-hour silence (W-06, W-07).
Medium design limits:
- Severity uses level % only. It ignores stock on the pasture, tank capacity and consumption, so T2 in an empty pasture is listed above T4, the leaking tank 45 heifers drink from (W-14, W-16).
- A silent tank last seen at 8% and falling is only "serious" (W-12).
- Conflicting duplicate timestamps are resolved by file order (W-04).
- A moved portable tank produces a false cross-pasture leak alarm (W-11).
Low: an exact 30.0-point drop is lost to floating-point error (W-13); a refill inside the window hides a 40-point fall (W-03); the tile breaks on tank IDs that contain a space (B-03); an unknown pasture prints "(undefined)" (W-15).
All repros are in one file, which runs clean (22 MISMATCH, 10 MATCH controls, 0 threw). No tracked repo file was changed.
trace:
SOURCE: data/water.csv rows (tank_id, pasture_id, time 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' with no timezone, level_pct), 6-hourly for September. meta.csv as_of=2026-09-30T18:00.

PARSE: parseCSV (exceptions.js:22-34) turns level_pct into a number when +v is not NaN. Otherwise it stays a string: '' for blank, 'ERR' for error codes. time stays a string.

SUMMARY: waterStatus(water, asOf) (exceptions.js:39-52):
- Groups rows by tank_id only (Map in first-appearance order). There is no tanks master, so a tank exists only if it has rows.
- Sorts each tank's rows by time with String.localeCompare (:43).
- last = the last sorted row. level = last.level_pct. pasture = last.pasture_id (the last row wins if the pasture changed).
- dayAgo = the latest row whose time is at least 1 day before last.time (:45). This is anchored to the last reading, not to as_of, and has no upper bound on age.
- drop24h = dayAgo.level - last.level, or 0 when there is no such row (:49).
- silentHours = (as_of - last.time) in hours, which goes negative for future rows (:48).

RULES: findExceptions (exceptions.js:101-116). For each tank:
- where = "Tank <id> (<pName[pasture]>[, <groups with an open move in that pasture> here now])".
- Rules are checked in order and only the first match is reported:
  1. silentHours >= 24: serious, "No reading for <round(h)> hours; last level <L>%", action "Check the tank by eye today, then the sensor battery and signal". The level is not judged after this (continue).
  2. drop24h >= 30: critical, "Dropped <round(d)> points in 24 hours, now <L>%", action "Check for a leak or a stuck float; haul water if it can't be fixed today".
  3. level < 25: critical, "Down to <L>% full", action "Check the float and the supply line today".
  4. level < 40: warning, "<L>% full", action "Look at it on the next pass".
- All rows are sorted by severity, then area (:158). Within a severity the order is tank first appearance, not urgency.

DISPLAY (app.js):
- Exception table (:61-70) prints subject, problem and action as above.
- Tile "Water tanks OK" (:46-55) = number of tanks from waterStatus minus the unique set of subject.split(" ")[1] over the Water rows.
- waterMultiples (:72-110), one mini chart per tank:
  - Heading: "no signal" when silentHours >= 24, otherwise "<level>%".
  - The line uses rows with time >= as_of - 7 days (:90).
  - last = the last row in that window (:92), then circle cx = x(last.time) (:93).
  - Silent tanks get a wash plus "no data" drawn from last.time to the right edge.
- The start line (:225) runs tiles, exceptionsTable, waterMultiples, grazingTimeline, gainStrip, budget, then rules. An exception thrown in waterMultiples stops every section after it.

COMMITTED DATA (observed with node):
- T2: last 11.8 → critical "Down to 11.8% full". Its pasture P2 Windmill has no open move.
- T4: 56 at 09-29T18:00 → 10 at 09-30T18:00, drop 46 → critical "Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%", "Heifers here now".
- T6: last row 09-29T00:00, 42 h before as_of → serious "No reading for 42 hours; last level 98.5%".
- T8: drop24h -19.5 (a refill), not flagged.
- Tile: "5 of 8, 3 need a look".
- 8 charts. T6 is headed "no signal".

findings.title: Water charts crash when a tank has no readings in the last 7 days, blanking every section after them
findings.location: app.js:90-93 (rows.filter window, then rows[rows.length-1].time); app.js:103 (rows.reduce with no initial value); app.js:225 (sections rendered in sequence, no isolation)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case B-01. The committed water.csv is served with every T6 row after 2026-09-22T12:00 removed (sensor dead 8 days 6 hours; older rows kept), loaded in headless Chromium.
findings.expected: No page error. 8 water charts, with T6 headed 'no signal' and a 'no readings in the last 7 days' panel. The grazing, gain and budget charts and the 12-row rules table still drawn. Report row 'No reading for 198 hours' (by hand: Sep 22 12:00 to Sep 30 18:00 = 8 d 6 h = 198 h).
findings.actual: page errors=["Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'time')"]; water charts=0; grazing svg=false; gain svg=false; budget svg=false; rules rows=0. The exception table, rendered earlier, still shows 'Serious Water Tank T6 (Cedar Draw) No reading for 198 hours; last level 100%'.
findings.consequence: This happens exactly when a sensor has been dead for more than a week, which is the case the silent-sensor rule exists for. The manager loses the water charts, the grazing rotation (who is overdue to move), the gain chart, the budget chart and table, and the rules table. To a reviewer the page looks broken.
findings.regression_test:
Playwright test (or a pure helper extracted from waterMultiples). Data: committed CSVs with T6 rows filtered to time <= '2026-09-22T12:00'. Assert:
- no pageerror
- document.querySelectorAll('#water .mini').length === 8
- the T6 heading text ends with 'no signal'
- #grazing svg, #gain svg and #budgetChart svg exist
- #rules tr count === 12
The values 8 and 12 come from the B-00 control run.
findings.proposed_fix:
In waterMultiples, when the 7-day window has no rows:
- draw a full-width wash with 'no readings since <fmtDate(t.lastTime)>'
- skip the path, circle and hover handler
- guard the reduce
Separately, wrap each section call at app.js:225 in try/catch that writes a visible 'This section could not be drawn' message, so one failure cannot blank the others.

findings.title: level_pct is never validated: 'ERR' hides a critical tank as healthy, a blank level becomes an 80-point 'leak'
findings.location: exceptions.js:30 (non-numbers stay strings); exceptions.js:47-49 (level and drop taken from the last row unchecked); exceptions.js:109-115 (comparisons against a string); app.js:82, 91, 93 (heading and SVG built from the raw value)
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, cases:
- W-10: inline 'T1,P1,2026-09-29T18:00,80 / T1,P1,2026-09-30T18:00,ERR'
- W-09: last row 'T1,P1,2026-09-30T18:00,' (blank level)
- B-05: committed data with T2's last row changed to ERR, in Chromium
findings.expected: The newest row has no valid level, so the tank's state is unknown and it is flagged (serious: 'last reading ERR is not a level; last good level 80% at Sep 29 18:00'). In B-05, T2 is still counted among those needing a look: tile '5 of 8, 3 need a look'. No 'ERR%' and no 'now %'.
findings.actual:
- W-10: level="ERR" drop24h=NaN; (no water alerts).
- B-05: T2's critical row disappears from the report. Tile 'WATER TANKS OK 6 of 8 2 need a look'. Heading 'T2 Windmill ERR%'. Console: 'Error: <path> attribute d: Expected number, "…45.9,79.6L254.0,NaN".'
- W-09: 'critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 80 points in 24 hours, now %'.
findings.consequence: Fault codes and blanks are common in tank-sensor exports. A fault code on the newest row turns the most urgent tank (T2 at 11.8%) into an all-clear: nobody goes and cattle run out of water. A truncated last row raises a false critical leak with a garbled 'now %' and sends a crew to haul water to a tank that is fine.
findings.regression_test:
Unit tests on findExceptions, with base = committed data:
(a) Base, plus water = rows 'T1,P1,2026-09-29T18:00,80' and 'T1,P1,2026-09-30T18:00,ERR'. Expect exactly 1 Water row for T1, severity 'serious', problem containing 'ERR' and '80%'.
(b) Same with a blank level. Expect the same serious row, and no row whose problem matches /Dropped|now %$/.
(c) Committed data with T2's 2026-09-30T18:00 row set to ERR. Expect a T2 Water row to exist. The level 11.8 at 2026-09-30T12:00... is not used: hand-check the file, T2's last good reading is at 2026-09-30T12:00 = 14.8.
findings.proposed_fix:
In waterStatus:
- Keep only rows where typeof level_pct === 'number' and 0 <= level_pct <= 100 as valid.
- Take level, drop and last-good time from valid rows.
- If the newest row by time is invalid, set state 'unknown' with badValue and badTime. findExceptions then emits a serious 'Last reading <v> at <time> is not a level; last good level <L>% at <t>'.
- Count unknown tanks as needing a look.
- waterMultiples skips invalid points and shows 'bad reading' in the heading.

findings.title: No tanks master table: a tank with zero readings is invisible to the alerts, the charts and the tile
findings.location: exceptions.js:39-42 (the tank list is built from water rows only); app.js:46, 55, 78; scripts/generate_data.py:39 (TANKS is defined but never written to a CSV)
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, cases:
- W-08: committed data with every T6 row removed, through findExceptions/waterStatus
- B-02: same data in Chromium
findings.expected: 8 tanks. T6 (Cedar Draw) flagged serious with 'no readings in this export'. Tile 'Water tanks OK 5 of 8, 3 need a look'.
findings.actual:
- W-08: 'tanks=7; critical | Tank T2 (Windmill) | Down to 11.8% full || critical | Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now) | Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%'.
- B-02: tile 'WATER TANKS OK 5 of 7 2 need a look'. 7 charts. No T6 anywhere.
findings.consequence: The silent-sensor rule only works while the dead sensor's old rows are still in the file. With a rolling export (for example the last 7 days) or a sensor that never reported, the tank vanishes. The page then shows a confident all-clear ('5 of 7 OK') for a tank nobody is watching. That is a misleading all-clear on water, the most time-critical area.
findings.regression_test:
Add a data/tanks.csv listing T1-T8 with their pastures, and remove T6 rows from water.csv. Expect:
- waterStatus length 8
- one T6 Water row, severity 'serious', problem containing 'No readings'
- tile text '5 of 8' and '3 need a look'
A tank_id in water.csv that is missing from tanks.csv produces a data warning.
findings.proposed_fix:
- Have generate_data.py write data/tanks.csv (tank_id, pasture_id, capacity_gal, has_sensor).
- Make waterStatus iterate the master and left-join readings. A tank with no readings gets state 'no data' and a serious alert.
- Add 'tanks' to the FILES lists in app.js and the tests, and document it in the README.

findings.title: Readings are ordered by string comparison of time: Excel-style or mixed timestamps pick the wrong 'last' reading
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, cases:
- W-05b: every time in the committed water.csv rewritten as Excel saves it in a US locale, e.g. '9/30/2026 18:00', '9/1/2026 6:00'
- W-05: three rows, the newest written '2026-09-30 18:00' (space), the others with T
findings.expected:
- W-05b: the same three rows as the committed data (same instants, same levels): T2 critical 11.8%, T4 critical 46-point drop, T6 serious 42 h.
- W-05: critical 'Down to 20% full' (the 18:00 reading is the newest).
findings.actual:
- W-05b: "T1 'last' row=9/9/2026 6:00 (89.8%); 8 rows: serious | Tank T1 (North Flat) | No reading for 516 hours; last level 89.8% || serious | Tank T2 (Windmill) | No reading for 516 hours; last level 82.6% || serious | Tank T3 ... "
- W-05: 'sorted order=2026-09-29T18:00 , 2026-09-30 18:00 , 2026-09-30T12:00; level used=75; (no water alerts)'.
findings.consequence: The README says 'To use real data, replace the CSVs with exports in the same columns'. Opening and saving in Excel is the usual way, and that reorders the dates. Every tank then reports 516 hours of silence with a 3-week-old level: T2 shows 82.6% while it is really at 11.8%, and the T4 leak is not shown. A single hand-entered row with a space hides a critical low tank.
findings.regression_test: Unit test: map the committed water rows through t => `${+MM}/${+DD}/${YYYY} ${+HH}:${mm}` and run findExceptions. Expect the same three Water rows as the committed data, i.e. ['critical|Tank T2 (Windmill)|Down to 11.8% full', 'critical|Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now)|Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%', 'serious|Tank T6 (Cedar Draw)|No reading for 42 hours; last level 98.5%'] (read off data/water.csv by hand). Alternatively, expect a visible 'unrecognised time format' data error. Never 8 silent rows.
findings.proposed_fix:
- Parse time once with a strict parser that accepts YYYY-MM-DD[T ]HH:MM[:SS] (and optionally m/d/yyyy h:mm), producing epoch ms.
- Reject anything else with a visible data error naming the file and row.
- Sort numerically, and compute silence and the drop window from the parsed numbers.

findings.title: drop24h baseline has no upper age limit: after a reading gap a multi-day change is reported as 'in 24 hours' and raises a false critical leak
findings.location: exceptions.js:45 (dayAgo = latest row at least 1 day before last, any age); exceptions.js:49; exceptions.js:110 (hard-coded 'in 24 hours' text); README and app.js:204 rule text
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case W-01. T1 rows: 2026-09-27T12:00 91, 2026-09-27T18:00 90, then a radio outage, 2026-09-30T12:00 56, 2026-09-30T18:00 54.
findings.expected: No water alert. Inside the true 24-h window (Sep 29 18:00 to Sep 30 18:00) the only readings are 56 → 54, i.e. 2 points in 6 h, and 54% is above 40%. At most, a drop text that says 36 points over 72 hours.
findings.actual: 'critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 36 points in 24 hours, now 54%'
findings.consequence: The day after the crew does what the dashboard says for T6 ('check ... the sensor battery and signal') and the sensor comes back, the same tank can be reported as a critical leak with 'haul water if it can't be fixed today'. That wastes crew time and erodes trust in the report. The '24 hours' wording in the README and rules table is untrue whenever readings are irregular.
findings.regression_test: With the W-01 rows and the committed moves/pastures, findExceptions returns 0 Water rows. Expected by hand: the window has max 56 and last 54, so a 2-point drop; level 54 >= 40.
findings.proposed_fix:
Bound the window to readings with last.time - 24h <= time <= last.time, in the same pasture as last. Then:
- drop = (max level in window) - last.level, or the max drawdown within the window
- the problem text gives the real span in hours
- if the window holds only the last reading, say 'can't judge the 24-hour change (no reading between <t1> and <t2>)' rather than 0
This is the same fix as the next finding.

findings.title: A fast drop is missed when no reading is 24 h older than the last one (new sensor, resumed sensor, export starting at midnight)
findings.location: exceptions.js:45 and :49 (no dayAgo row means drop24h = 0)
findings.expected: Critical: a drop of 45 points (95 → 50) within 24 hours. By hand, 45 >= 30.
findings.consequence: A tank losing about 2.5 points an hour sits at 50% with no alert. At that rate it would be under 25% about 10 hours later (by hand: (50-25)/2.5). It may be dry before the next morning's report. The leak rule is effectively off for the first day of any sensor's history.
findings.regression_test: W-02 rows: expect one Water row for T1, severity 'critical', problem containing '45 points'. With the windowed rule the text would be 'Dropped 45 points in 18 hours, now 50%'; 18 h = 00:00 to 18:00.
findings.proposed_fix: Same as the previous finding. Use the peak (or max drawdown) inside [last.time - 24h, last.time] instead of requiring a reading at least 24 h old. Report the actual span.

findings.title: Readings dated after as_of give negative silence and pass as fresh; one mistyped row hides a real 42-hour silence
findings.location: exceptions.js:48 (silentHours can be negative); exceptions.js:104; app.js:76, 90-93 (future point drawn past the plot edge)
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, cases:
- W-06: T1 rows 2026-09-29T18:00 80 and 2026-10-02T18:00 80
- W-07: committed data plus one row 'T6,P6,2026-10-29T00:00,95' (month typed 10 for 09)
- B-04: committed data plus 'T1,P1,2026-10-02T18:00,80', in Chromium
findings.expected:
- W-07: T6 still serious 'No reading for 42 hours' (by hand: Sep 29 00:00 to Sep 30 18:00 = 42 h), plus a data warning for the future-dated row.
- W-06: a data-quality alert; silentHours never negative.
- B-04: T1 not shown as a plain '80%'.
findings.actual:
- W-06: 'silentHours=-48; (no water alerts)'.
- W-07: 'T6 silentHours=-678; critical | Tank T2 ... || critical | Tank T4 ...'. T6 has disappeared.
- B-04: heading 'T1 North Flat 80%', last-point dot cx=319.14 (plot right edge 254).
findings.consequence: A manual tank-check row with the wrong month, or a sensor whose clock jumps ahead, suppresses the silent-sensor alert. This is a missed alert for a tank nobody has seen in nearly two days. The level shown is from 'the future' and nothing indicates it.
findings.regression_test:
- W-07 data: expect a serious T6 row with problem 'No reading for 42 hours; last level 98.5%' (98.5 is T6's 2026-09-29T00:00 value in data/water.csv), plus a row naming '2026-10-29'.
- W-06 data: expect a T1 row; waterStatus(...).silentHours >= 0 for every tank.
findings.proposed_fix:
- In waterStatus, set aside rows with time > as_of and do not use them for level, drop or silence.
- Emit a data-quality row ('Reading dated <t> is after the as-of time; check the sensor clock or the entry').
- Clamp chart x to the plot area.

findings.title: Conflicting readings at the same timestamp: the alert depends on row order in the file
findings.location: exceptions.js:43-44 (stable sort; the last of equal times wins)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case W-04. T1: 2026-09-29T18:00 80, then two rows at 2026-09-30T18:00 (78 and 20), run in both orders.
findings.expected: The same alerts for both orders, plus a 'conflicting readings' flag. A conservative rule uses the lower value (20%).
findings.actual: 'order 78-then-20: critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 60 points in 24 hours, now 20%   |   order 20-then-78: (no water alerts)'
findings.consequence: A re-sent sensor packet, or a manual check entered alongside the sensor value, decides between 'critical, haul water' and nothing, depending on which line happens to come last.
findings.regression_test: For both orders, expect the same Water rows: one critical T1 row with 'now 20%' (80 - 20 = 60 points by hand), plus a warning naming both values 78% and 20%.
findings.proposed_fix: Group rows by (tank, parsed time). If the levels differ by more than 1 point, flag 'readings disagree' and use the lower level. If they are equal, drop the duplicate.

findings.title: A silent tank last seen nearly empty and falling is only 'serious', ranked below every critical row
findings.location: exceptions.js:104-108 (silence always gives serious and the last level/trend is discarded via continue)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case W-12. T1: 2026-09-28T18:00 60, 2026-09-29T06:00 30, 2026-09-29T12:00 8, then nothing (30 h before as_of).
findings.expected: Critical. The last known level is 8%, under the 25% line, after a 52-point fall in 18 h (by hand: 60 - 8), and there has been no reading for 30 h. The tank is likely dry.
findings.actual: 'serious | Tank T1 (North Flat) | No reading for 30 hours; last level 8%'
findings.consequence: The tank most likely to be dry (and whose sensor may have lost power along with the pump or solar) is listed below an empty-pasture low tank. Its action is 'check by eye today' rather than 'go now, take water'.
findings.regression_test: W-12 data: expect one T1 row with severity 'critical' and problem containing '30 hours' and '8%'. Keep: a silent tank whose last level was 98.5% (T6 in the committed data) stays serious.
findings.proposed_fix: If the tank is silent and its last valid level < waterCritical, or its last known 24-h drop >= waterDropPts, emit critical with 'No reading for N hours; last seen L% and falling' and the action 'Go now; take water if it's dry'. Update the README's 'isn't judged' line.

findings.title: Severity uses level % alone: it ignores stock on the pasture, tank capacity and consumption, so an empty-pasture tank outranks a leaking tank 45 heifers drink from
findings.location: exceptions.js:109-115 (level/drop thresholds only); exceptions.js:158 (within a severity, order is tank file order); no capacity or head data in water.csv
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, cases:
- W-14: committed data
- W-16: TA in P7 (Cows here now) and TB in P2 (empty), both at 38%
findings.expected:
Rows where stock is drinking come first or are rated higher.
- W-14: first Water row is Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now). moves.csv rows with no out_date put the Cows in P7, Heifers in P4 and Yearlings in P3, so P2 Windmill is empty.
- W-16: TA ranked or rated above TB.
findings.actual:
- W-14: 'critical | Tank T2 (Windmill) | Down to 11.8% full || critical | Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now) | Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10% || serious | Tank T6 ...'
- W-16: 'warning | Tank TB (Windmill) | 38% full || warning | Tank TA (South Divide, Cows here now) | 38% full'
findings.consequence:
The top row of the report sends the crew to an empty pasture. The leaking tank that 45 heifers depend on is second. A 38% tank with 180 pairs on it gets 'Look at it on the next pass'.
Illustration with assumed figures, which are not in the data: a 1,000-gal tank at 38% holds 380 gal. At roughly 20 gal per pair per day, 180 pairs drink about 150 gal/h, so that is about 2.5 h without inflow.
The data model cannot say whether water is actually short.
findings.regression_test:
- Committed data: expect the first Water row's subject to contain 'Tank T4'.
- W-16 rows: expect the first Water row to be TA, or TA's severity to be higher than TB's.
- After capacity_gal and gal/head/day exist: a 1,000-gal tank at 38% with 180 head at 20 gal/day gives hours_left = 380 / (180 × 20 / 24) = 2.53 h, computed by hand.
findings.proposed_fix:
Short term:
- Sort Water rows with stocked pastures first.
- Show the head count in 'here now'.
- Make 'critical' for a low level conditional on stock being present or due within N days; otherwise 'serious: fix before stock goes back in'.
Longer term: add capacity_gal (tanks.csv) and a per-class gal/head/day table, and alert on hours of water left. Until then, state this limitation in the README.

findings.title: A tank whose pasture_id changes (moved portable trough) is compared across placements and raises a false leak
findings.location: exceptions.js:41 (series keyed by tank_id only); exceptions.js:47 (pasture taken from the last row); exceptions.js:45 (baseline can come from another pasture)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case W-11. T9: 2026-09-29T18:00 in P1 at 90; 2026-09-30T12:00 in P3 at 15; 2026-09-30T18:00 in P3 at 55.
findings.expected: No water alert. The 90% reading was in another pasture, and 55% now is above 40%.
findings.actual: 'critical | Tank T9 (Sand Hills, Yearlings here now) | Dropped 35 points in 24 hours, now 55%'
findings.consequence:
A false critical leak alarm the day a portable trough is moved with the yearlings.
Inferred, not reproduced: two different tanks sharing an id across pastures would be merged, and one tank's silence could be masked by the other's readings.
findings.regression_test: W-11 rows: expect 0 Water rows. By hand, only the P3 readings 15 → 55 count, and that is a rise.
findings.proposed_fix: Key series by (tank_id, pasture_id) placement, or start a new baseline at a pasture change. Once tanks.csv exists, validate that each reading's pasture matches the tank's current placement.

findings.title: An exact 30.0-point drop is missed by floating-point subtraction
findings.location: exceptions.js:49 and :109 (raw float subtraction compared with >= 30)
findings.expected: Critical 'Dropped 30 points in 24 hours, now 50.1%'. By hand 80.1 - 50.1 = 30.0, which meets '30+ points'.
findings.actual: 'drop24h=29.999999999999993; (no water alerts)'. Separately, 48 of the one-decimal level pairs 70.0-100.0 that are exactly 30.0 apart compute below 30 (node scan).
findings.consequence: Rare. A threshold-exact leak is not flagged, and the rule disagrees with its own documentation at the boundary.
findings.regression_test: Rows 80.1 → 50.1 over 24 h: expect one critical Water row with 'Dropped 30 points'.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare the rounded value, e.g. Math.round(drop * 10) / 10 >= R.waterDropPts. Levels are recorded to 0.1.

findings.title: A large fall inside the window that refills before the last reading is not seen (endpoint comparison)
findings.location: exceptions.js:49 (dayAgo level minus last level only)
findings.expected: The 40-point fall (90 → 50) within the last 24 h is reported, at least as a warning (intermittent float or leak).
findings.consequence: An intermittently sticking float, or a leak the supply only partly keeps up with, goes unreported until it fails outright. The water is there now, so this is low urgency.
findings.regression_test:
W-03 rows: expect one T1 row mentioning 40 points (max drawdown 90 - 50 by hand).
Evidence that no new false alarms are added: on the committed data, the worst 24-h drawdown over the whole month for the healthy tanks is 18.2 points (T8). Node output: 'T8 ... worst24hDrawdownAllMonth 18.2'. That is under 30.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the max drawdown within the bounded 24-h window. This shares code with the drop-baseline fixes above.

findings.title: The 'Water tanks OK' tile re-parses the tank id from the alert text and miscounts tank ids that contain a space
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case B-03. Committed data with T2 renamed 'Well 2' and T4 renamed 'Well 4', in Chromium.
findings.expected: Tile 'Water tanks OK 5 of 8, 3 need a look' (Well 2, Well 4, T6).
findings.actual: tile='WATER TANKS OK 6 of 8 2 need a look' (the report itself correctly lists Well 2, Well 4 and T6).
findings.consequence: With real tank names such as 'Well 2' or 'Spring tank', the headline tile overstates how many tanks are fine and disagrees with the report below it.
findings.regression_test: B-03 data: the tile contains '5 of 8' and '3 need a look'. Expected: 8 tanks, of which 3 have Water rows, counted by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the water ex() rows carry key: t.tank, or build the set from the waterStatus results using the same predicate, instead of parsing display text.

findings.title: A tank in a pasture missing from pastures.csv is labelled 'Tank T9 (undefined)'
findings.location: exceptions.js:103 (pName[t.pasture] with no fallback); app.js:82 (names[t.pasture] in the chart heading, inferred, not run)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs, case W-15. T9 in P9 at 22 then 20.
findings.expected: Subject 'Tank T9 (P9)' or 'unknown pasture P9', plus a data warning.
findings.consequence: The crew is told to check a tank 'in undefined'. That is a credibility hit in a portfolio piece and a real problem when the pasture really isn't in the list (a headquarters trap, say).
findings.regression_test: W-15 rows: the subject equals 'Tank T9 (P9)' or contains 'P9', and does not contain 'undefined'.
findings.proposed_fix: Use pName[t.pasture] ?? t.pasture (and the same in app.js:82, 104), and add a data-quality row for an unknown pasture_id.

silentHours uses one consistent clock. as_of and the readings are both timezone-less strings parsed the same way, so the hour difference does not depend on the viewer's zone (except across a DST change). Checked only under TZ=UTC in node and in the default Chromium zone, not in other zones.
